summary: Self-improving agent loop that runs ML experiments, keeps only changes that beat the current benchmark, and rolls back failures. Released March 2026, 66k stars.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the run-loop-with-rollback concept partially maps to AgentForge's plan revision and remediation stages, but AutoResearch targets ML training optimization (single train.py file), not software engineering orchestration. AgentForge already has skill distillation as its learning mechanism.

summary: Microsoft merged AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into a single production-ready framework with graph-based multi-agent orchestration, Agent2Agent (A2A), and MCP support. GA April 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents (claude/codex), not SDK-based agents. The handoff/graph orchestration pattern doesn't apply to the ProcessRunner architecture. A2A is an external protocol, not relevant to the internal deterministic state machine.

summary: LangGraph reached 1.0 LTS in October 2025 with durable execution, streaming, human-in-the-loop, and checkpointing as stable features. LangChain 1.0 refocuses on rapid prototyping.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already ships all the capabilities LangGraph 1.0 highlights: deterministic state machine (stateMachine.ts), SSE streaming (runEventEmitter.ts), human-in-the-loop (AwaitingPlanApproval), checkpoint-like worktrees. No gap to close.

source: Mem0 State of AI Agent Memory 2026 Report
summary: Benchmark report on agent memory architectures in 2026: three-tier model (working/episodic/semantic), cross-session retrieval, token-efficient hierarchical extraction showing ~26% accuracy improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the episodic/cross-run memory gap is real for AgentForge but already tracked by HID-188 (feat: inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts). The executor skill injection gap (executor prompts don't receive skills yet) is part of HID-188 scope.

summary: Uses a pool of different LLM agents within MCTS planning to increase rollout diversity and improve multi-step reasoning via speculative branching.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge deliberately rejected speculative/parallel execution as premature (noted in CLAUDE.md Phase 2). Multi-model panels also evaluated and rejected as cost multipliers. This requires parallel agent infrastructure that does not exist and was deferred.

summary: E-mem uses a master agent for global planning with uncompressed episodic memory contexts; ShardMemo uses masked mixture-of-experts routing across memory shards for efficient retrieval.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — episodic memory for AgentForge is tracked by HID-188. These papers offer architectural inspiration for implementation but do not add a new capability gap. Backlog already has this theme covered.

summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' in February 2026 and articulated core skills: spec design (detailed requirements), diff review (architectural correctness), eval design (verifiable feedback loops), and security oversight. agents.md is a conventions file for coding agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the spec/eval design loop maps to AgentForge's plan→review→implement cycle. The agents.md convention (structured constraints in a markdown file per-repo) is similar to AgentForge's repos.config.json and issue-template approach. No clear new gap, but useful framing for future prompt engineering.
